thought.text: I've identified concrete bugs in `docker-compose.dev.yml`. Let me examine the exact sections.

reasoning_content:
The heredoc terminator is on the same line as content: `sslmode=disable EOF\n` — so the heredoc never terminates properly? Actually let me look. The line is `[qonnectra] host=db ... sslmode=disable EOF`. There is no newline before EOF, so the heredoc delimiter `EOF` isn't the whole line - it's at the end of the content line. That means the heredoc doesn't get terminated, so `cat` reads... wait but the script ran fine when I executed it (RC=0).

Actually in the stored command, the `[qonnectra] ... EOF\n` line has EOF at end but not alone on the line. Hmm, bash heredoc requires the delimiter alone on a line. Here `EOF` is at the end of the content line, so the heredoc continues reading until a line containing only `EOF`. There's no such line, so cat reads the rest of the script. That would consume everything...

Wait but when I ran `sh /cmd.sh` where cmd.sh contained those lines, RC=0 and it started. Let me re-examine. Actually when I ran it the heredoc content line had `... sslmode=disable EOF` and then next line `mkdir...`. Since EOF isn't alone, the heredoc would consume all subsequent lines until EOF-of-file, and `cat` would write those to pg_service.conf. That's clearly broken. Then after that, the `cat` command completes at EOF. The `&&` chain... Actually if heredoc terminates at EOF of input, cat succeeds, then `mkdir -p /var/www/data/qgis && ...`? No — those lines were consumed as heredoc content, not executed.

Hmm, but my test showed RC=0 and it started. Let me re-check: in my test `sh /cmd.sh` where /cmd.sh is exactly the extracted command. Actually the output was empty and RC=0, I only saw "RC=0". It may have just run cat and consumed the rest. That means the container exits quickly (tail -f /dev/null is never reached) → exit 0 → restart loop! That matches "Restarting (0)".

So the QGIS bug is the heredoc terminator in the dev compose (inline `EOF` at end of line instead of on its own line). In docker-compose.yml (production), they correctly used `printf`.

Also the nginx bug: dev compose mounts ./nginx/nginx.conf to /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf (wrong; should mount nginx.conf to /etc/nginx/nginx.conf and default.conf to conf.d/default.conf).

Wait - let me re-read the dev compose nginx volumes:
```
volumes:
  - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
```
Yes! Only one mount, and it maps nginx.conf (the http block) to conf.d/default.conf which is included inside http block. That's the bug causing "worker_processes directive is not allowed here". The production compose correctly mounts both.

Tileserver: config.json references germany.mbtiles which doesn't exist (user-generated, documented as required). So tileserver restart is expected due to missing mbtiles - documented as user-provided. But it's a documented prerequisite.

So there are bugs in the dev compose file. The guide's primary Quick Start uses `docker-compose up -d --build` which defaults to docker-compose.yml (production). Let me consider using the production compose instead. But it also has issues: needs .env with domains, Caddyfile.production with Let's Encrypt (won't work for localhost). Actually production uses real domains. The guide Quick Start says create .env then docker-compose up. Hmm.

Given the task: "Install the assigned software and report the outcome based on objective evidence." The core app (backend+frontend+db) is running. But nginx (reverse proxy) and qgis-server are broken due to compose bugs, and tileserver needs user-generated mbtiles.

I should fix the dev compose to get the full stack working, since I've diagnosed the bugs. But wait - should I attribute failure to DOCUMENTATION? The task wants a successful installation if possible. Let me fix the clear bugs to complete installation.

Let me fix:
1. nginx mount in docker-compose.dev.yml — map correctly.
2. qgis heredoc in docker-compose.dev.yml.

These are installation-level fixes (the compose is part of the repo). The guide says use docker-compose up. Let me make the fixes minimal.

Actually, am I allowed to modify the repo? The task says "You may perform actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out the installation." Fixing bugs in the compose to make installation succeed is reasonable.

But also consider: maybe I should try the production compose method first before modifying. Actually the guide's Getting Started says `docker-compose up -d --build` in deployment — that uses docker-compose.yml (production). It has the same db Dockerfile issue (fixed) and nginx is correct, but Caddyfile.production uses real domains + Let's Encrypt which won't resolve for localhost. Production also lacks the tileserver issue being fatal (it restarts). Let me not overcomplicate; the dev compose is the documented local/docker method.

Let me fix the dev compose nginx mount and qgis heredoc. Let me also check tileserver - the mbtiles is user-generated per docs, so tileserver can't fully work without generating tiles (Java/Planetiler, ~3GB). That's documented as an optional asset. The app might fall back to OSM. Let me focus on nginx+qgis.

Let me view the dev compose qgis section and nginx section.
